name: Hanukkah
seo_title: Hanukkah Charcuterie Board Ideas: 7 Kosher-Style Boards
description: 7 Hanukkah charcuterie board ideas, kosher-style: a latke and lox board, a deli meat board, a bagel brunch board, a blue-and-white cheese board, a pareve mezze board, party cups and a gelt dessert board.
answer: Go kosher-style: a dairy board (cheese, smoked salmon, latkes) or a meat board (beef salami, pastrami, no pork), never both. Shape it like a menorah and plan about 2 oz each per guest.

ideas.title: The Latke and Lox Board
ideas.text: Crisp latkes with sour cream and applesauce, smoked salmon with whipped cream cheese, capers and red onion, a sharp cheddar and a soft goat cheese, plus cucumbers and rye crisps. Every item is dairy or pareve, so nothing on it is meat.

ideas.title: The Deli Meat Board
ideas.text: Beef salami, pastrami and smoked turkey with deli mustard, half-sour pickles, olives, hummus and baba ganoush, with rye and challah. No cheese or butter on this one, so it can follow a meat meal.

ideas.title: The Bagel and Lox Brunch Board
ideas.link_text: How to build a bagel board
ideas.text: Bagels, two or three cream cheeses, smoked salmon, capers, red onion, tomato and cucumber. Skip any bacon to keep it kosher-style, and set out everything but the fresh items the night before.
ideas.on_it: Bagels · cream cheeses · smoked salmon · capers · red onion · tomato · cucumber · fruit

ideas.title: The Blue-and-White Cheese Board
ideas.text: White cheeses with blue and white fruit: feta, goat cheese and brie with blueberries, white grapes and cucumber, plus honey and plain crackers. Lay it out in the shape of a menorah or a Star of David (see the shapes below).
ideas.on_it: Feta · goat cheese · brie · blueberries · white grapes · cucumber · honey · water crackers

ideas.title: The Mezze Board (Pareve)
ideas.text: Hummus, muhammara, falafel, dolmas, dates and pistachios, with nothing from meat or dairy. That makes it an easy side board next to either a dairy meal or a meat meal. If guests keep strictly kosher, check the certification on each product.

ideas.title: Hanukkah Party Cups
ideas.for: Meat cups or dairy cups · 24+ cups
ideas.text: Individual cups for a party where people stand and mingle. Make meat cups with beef salami and pickles, or dairy cups with cheese and crackers, but don't put meat and cheese in the same cup.
ideas.on_it: Meat cups: beef salami, pickles, olives, rye crackers · Dairy cups: cheddar, goat cheese, grapes, crackers

ideas.title: The Gelt and Sufganiyot Dessert Board
ideas.text: Chocolate gelt, jelly doughnut holes, rugelach, halvah, dried apricots and dates, pistachios and a bowl of honey. Choose a pareve (dairy-free) chocolate if it follows a meat meal.

shapes.name: Menorah Board
steps: On a long rectangular board, stand nine breadsticks or long crackers in a row, with the middle one (the shamash) taller than the rest.
Put a cube of cheddar or a dried apricot at the top of each one as the flame.
Build the base with folded smoked salmon or salami, then fill the gaps with grapes, olives and nuts.

shapes.name: Star of David Board
steps: On a round board, make two triangles from rye crisps or pretzel rods, one pointing up and one pointing down.
Set a bowl of whipped cream cheese or hummus in the center.
Line the triangles in blue and white: blueberries, white cheese cubes and cucumber slices.

plan.what: Decide on a dairy board or a meat board, and ask guests who keep kosher which brands and certifications they need.
Buy gelt, crackers, nuts, dried fruit and jarred items. They keep.
Buy smoked salmon, cheese or deli meats, and fresh fruit.
Fry the latkes, cool them on a rack, slice fruit and cucumbers and fill the bowls. Cover and chill.
Take hard cheese out of the fridge and build the board. Reheat the latkes at 375°F and add them last.

faq.q: Can a charcuterie board be kosher?
faq.a: Yes, with kosher-certified products and one rule: meat and dairy don't share a board. Build a dairy board (cheese, smoked fish, latkes) or a meat board (beef or turkey salami, pastrami), not both, and skip pork and shellfish. If guests keep strictly kosher, ask which certifications they use and serve on new or dedicated boards.

faq.q: What goes on a Hanukkah charcuterie board?
faq.a: Latkes with sour cream and applesauce, smoked salmon with cream cheese and capers, two cheeses, rye crisps, fruit, and something sweet like chocolate gelt or doughnut holes. Blue and white foods (blueberries, white cheese, cucumber) make it look the part.

faq.q: Why are fried foods eaten on Hanukkah?
faq.a: Hanukkah remembers the story of a small jar of oil that burned for eight days, so foods fried in oil, like latkes and sufganiyot (jelly doughnuts), are the tradition.

faq.q: How much should I buy for a Hanukkah party?
faq.a: As an appetizer before a meal, plan about 2 oz of cheese and 2 oz of meat per guest, plus 6 to 8 crackers. If the board is the party food, plan 3 oz of each and 10 to 12 crackers; if it's dinner, 4 oz of each. From 20 guests, add 10%.

faq.q: Can I make latkes ahead for the board?
faq.a: Yes. Fry them earlier in the day, cool them on a rack, then reheat them in a single layer at 375°F for about 8 to 10 minutes so they crisp again. Add them to the board last so they stay warm and crunchy.

faq.q: Is smoked salmon dairy or meat?
faq.a: Neither. Fish is pareve, so smoked salmon is usually served on a dairy board with cream cheese. Some people who keep kosher don't serve fish together with meat, so keep it off the meat board.
Pareve foods contain no meat or dairy, so they can be eaten with either. Fruit, vegetables, nuts, eggs, fish and most breads and crackers are usually pareve, but check the label for milk or butter.

faq.q: What's a good Hanukkah brunch board?
faq.a: A bagel and lox board: bagels, cream cheeses, smoked salmon, capers, red onion, tomato and cucumber, with fruit and latkes on the side. It's a dairy board, so leave off any meat.

faq.q: How much does a Hanukkah charcuterie board cost?
faq.a: Before a meal, plan about $3 to $5 per guest on a budget and $5 to $8 for a standard board, so roughly $35 to $60 or $60 to $95 for 12 guests. Splurge cheeses and meats run $12 or more per guest. Store and region change the total.

faq.q: How far ahead can I make a Hanukkah charcuterie board?
faq.a: Shop for crackers, nuts and jars a week ahead and for cheese, meat and fruit 2 days ahead. The morning of, slice the cheese and fold the meats, then cover and chill. Build the board in the last hour, reheating the latkes at 375°F for 8 to 10 minutes and adding them last, adding crackers last so they stay crisp.

mistakes.lead: Putting meat and cheese on one board.
mistakes.text: If anyone at the party keeps kosher, make a dairy board or a meat board, not one board with both. Fish and vegetables are pareve and can go on either.
Most supermarket salami and pepperoni contain pork. Look for all-beef salami, ideally with a kosher certification.
Latkes go soggy on the board. Reheat them at 375°F and add them last, right before guests eat.

mistakes.lead: Guessing what strictly kosher guests need.
mistakes.text: Ask which certifications they use, and serve on new or dedicated boards and knives.

ahead: 2 weeks: settle dairy or meat, and check which kosher certifications guests need
1 week: gelt, crackers, nuts, dried fruit and jars
The morning of: fry the latkes and cool them on a rack; slice fruit and cucumbers; fill the bowls
last: Reheat the latkes at 375°F for 8 to 10 minutes and add them last
Smoked salmon stays in the fridge until the board goes out
